record.paper_title: Formal languages and arithmetic theories: recent results and open problems
record.original_question: Let p be an integer at least 2 and Sigma = {0, ..., p - 1}. For a deterministic finite automaton A over Sigma^(k+1) that recognizes synchronized encodings of k+1 words, define the universal projection of L(A) to Sigma^k to be the set of k-tuples (w1, ..., wk) such that for every possible (k+1)-st word wk+1 over Sigma, after padding and convolution so that all words have the same length, the tuple (w1, ..., wk, wk+1) is accepted by A. Is there a syntactically defined subclass A of deterministic finite automata such that, for every automaton A in this subclass, the universal projection of L(A) can always be represented by a nondeterministic finite automaton whose size is at most exponential in |A|?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2. Is there a syntactic subclass A of DFA such that for any A ∈ A over Σk+1, the universal projection of L(A) to Σk can be represented by an NFA of size exponential in |A|?
Given a DFA A over Σk+1, encoding assignments of k + 1 variables, eliminating a universally quantified variable computes the universal projection of L(A)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer $p \geq 2$ and let $\Sigma = \{0,1,\dots,p-1\}$. For words $w_1,\dots,w_m \in \Sigma^*$, let $\langle w_1,\dots,w_m\rangle \in (\Sigma^m)^*$ denote their synchronized (convolution) encoding: each $w_i$ is right-padded (with a fixed pad symbol or, equivalently, with $0$) to the common length $\max_j |w_j|$, and the resulting padded words are read in parallel, producing a single word over the alphabet $\Sigma^m$ whose $j$-th letter is the $m$-tuple of the $j$-th letters of the padded words.

Let $A$ be a deterministic finite automaton (DFA) over the alphabet $\Sigma^{k+1}$, and let $L(A) \subseteq (\Sigma^{k+1})^*$ be the language it recognizes. Define the universal projection of $L(A)$ onto $\Sigma^k$ as
$$\Pi^{\forall}(L(A)) = \{(w_1,\dots,w_k) \in (\Sigma^*)^k : \text{for every } w_{k+1} \in \Sigma^*,\ \langle w_1,\dots,w_k,w_{k+1}\rangle \in L(A)\}.$$

(Here $\Pi^{\forall}(L(A))$ is viewed, via the same convolution encoding, as a language over $\Sigma^k$.)

In general, while complementing $A$ does not blow up its size and existential projection produces an NFA of size linear in $|A|$, the universal projection is obtained by complementing the existential projection of the complement, and the resulting NFA can have size doubly exponential in $|A|$.

Question: Does there exist a syntactically defined subclass $\mathcal{A}$ of DFAs such that, for every $A \in \mathcal{A}$ over $\Sigma^{k+1}$, the universal projection $\Pi^{\forall}(L(A))$ can be represented by a nondeterministic finite automaton (NFA) of size at most singly exponential in $|A|$?
